clue.text: Supporting attempt to enforce prohibition

parts.note: to be supporting something is to be for it
a bid is an attempt, as in a bid for freedom

explanation.surface: Campaigners make a supportive attempt to have alcohol prohibition enforced.
explanation.definitionFit: To ban something is to put a prohibition on it and see it is kept.

clue.text: Dull-witted as some Angles?

definitions.meaning: describing some angles in geometry, those greater than ninety degrees; the capital A suggests the Germanic tribe

explanation.definitionFit: Obtuse means both mentally slow and, of an angle, between ninety and one hundred and eighty degrees.

clue.text: Cry when friend replaces first brace of ducks? What a commotion!

indicators.note: the friend takes the place of the first two O-shaped ducks

parts.note: boo-hoo is the sound of crying
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A friend's cry over two ducks causes quite a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a zero in cricket, so a brace of ducks is OO; the first pair in BOOHOO gives way to ALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballyhoo is noisy fuss or uproar.

clue.text: Comparatively ominous situation for the indecisive type

indicators.note: the word for more ominous is the place where the word the is situated, so it holds it

parts.note: direr means more dire, more ominous

explanation.surface: A rather more threatening situation is unwelcome for someone who cannot decide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'situation for' is an unusual container signal: the more ominous word is where 'the' is situated, the place it lives.
explanation.definitionFit: A ditherer hesitates and cannot make up their mind.

clue.text: New environment for a child endlessly unpredictable

indicators.note: an environment surrounds what lives in it, so one piece is wrapped round the others

parts.note: fresh means new

indicators.note: the word for child loses its final letter

parts.note: a kid is a child

explanation.surface: A fresh setting proves endlessly unpredictable for a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'environment for' reads as a setting in the surface, but it is the container signal; 'endlessly' trims the child word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something freakish is odd and erratic, so nobody can foresee it.

clue.text: Pay soldiers to be liveried attendants

parts.note: to foot a bill is to pay it
men are soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: Soldiers are paid to serve as uniformed servants.
explanation.definitionFit: Footmen are uniformed male servants in a grand house.

clue.text: Old bar aims to develop — the food is divine!

indicators.note: developing changes the form of these letters into something new

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old pub plans to build up its menu with divine dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambrosia was the food of the Greek gods.

clue.text: Press function exhibiting craftsman's output

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them
to work is to function, to operate

explanation.surface: A printing press works, showing off an artisan's products.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironwork is decorative metal made by a smith.

clue.text: Child's toy, an obsession for adults

definitions.meaning: a stick with a horse's head that a child rides
a favourite topic that a grown-up keeps returning to

explanation.definitionFit: The name is both a stick toy and a pet subject someone harps on about.

clue.text: Dagger securing end of Becket in T. S. Eliot version

indicators.note: the final letter of Becket goes in among the rearranged letters of the poet's name
a version of the name is a fresh rendering of its letters
the end of Becket is its last letter

explanation.surface: A dagger figures in T. S. Eliot's version of Becket's death, Murder in the Cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version' rearranges TSELIOT, and 'end of' takes T from Becket to go in among those letters. Thomas Becket was stabbed in Canterbury Cathedral, the subject of Eliot's play.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a short, slim-bladed knife for stabbing.

clue.text: Sailor's brother returns to hold

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor; with the 's it gives three letters

indicators.note: returns means the short word for brother is read backwards

explanation.surface: A sailor's brother comes home to keep hold of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's of Sailor's supplies a real letter here, which is unusual; 'returns' turns only the brother.
explanation.definitionFit: To absorb something is to take it in and keep it.

clue.text: Instant means to cross peak used by drivers in a hurry

definitions.text: used by drivers in a hurry

indicators.note: the peak goes across the gap between the other two pieces, sitting in their middle

parts.note: mo is short for moment, an instant
a way is a means, a method
a tor is a rocky hill or peak

explanation.surface: A quick route over a summit suits motorists who are pressed for time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cross' means the peak spans the join between the other two pieces, landing in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorway is a fast British road for long-distance traffic, the equivalent of a freeway.

clue.text: Soldiers rush to load again

parts.note: RE, Royal Engineers, is a British army corps of soldiers
to charge is to rush forward at an enemy

explanation.surface: Troops charge forward and then stop to reload their weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Recharging a gun means putting a fresh load in it.

clue.text: Rickety farm animal on chain

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
a shackle is a chain or fetter

explanation.surface: A tottering old sheep tethered by a chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramshackle means falling apart, badly built.

clue.text: Building work man goes round, riding in carriage?

indicators.note: going round turns the man's name back to front

parts.note: Sam is a man's name
riding in a train carriage is being on the railway, ON plus RY, the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A builder walks round a construction site and then rides home in a train carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes round' turns the man's name back to front. The question mark flags the loose reading of riding in a carriage as being on the railway, RY being its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Masonry is stonework or brickwork laid by builders.

clue.text: Inferior translation used on picture

parts.note: inferior suggests poor quality, but it means lower down: words of translation printed below a film

explanation.definitionFit: A film caption showing translated dialogue at the foot of the screen.

clue.text: Final drink that may go to one's head

definitions.meaning: a last alcoholic drink before bed

definitions.text: that may go to one's head
definitions.meaning: headwear for bed, a soft cap worn while asleep

explanation.definitionFit: The name covers both a bedtime tipple and a cap worn in bed.

clue.text: Striking individual given a big kiss

definitions.meaning: someone who strikes, a person who slaps
a loud smacking kiss, in informal British usage

explanation.definitionFit: A smack is a blow and also a loud kiss, so one who smacks and a smacking kiss share the name.

clue.text: Gives faulty advice to Yorkshire beauty queen, say

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken out loud

parts.note: Miss Leeds would be a beauty queen from Leeds, a Yorkshire city

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire pageant winner is given bad tips.
explanation.definitionFit: To mislead someone is to steer them wrong with bad guidance.

clue.text: Two outstanding features of toast

indicators.note: two means the facial feature is written twice

parts.note: a chin is a feature that sticks out from the face

explanation.surface: Two prominent qualities stand out in a speech raising a glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Chin-chin is a cheery drinking salutation, like cheers.

clue.text: Funny prose of parodist

indicators.note: something funny is odd, so the letters are made odd by rearranging

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Comic writing by a satirist.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoofer is one who mocks something by imitation.

clue.text: Sweet even now wedged between piano keys

parts.note: p is the musical marking for piano, softly

indicators.note: wedged between means pushed into the middle of the outer letters

parts.note: A and E are musical keys
still means even now, as in it is still raining

explanation.surface: A sweet that is still lodged between the keys of a piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wedged between' puts STILL inside P and A on one side and E on the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastille is a small chewy sweet or lozenge.

clue.text: Sounds like one who flogs spirits

indicators.note: the clue states plainly that what follows is to be spoken

parts.note: a licker is one who beats or thrashes, as in a licking

explanation.surface: A salesman who peddles strong drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Flogs suggests selling, but it means beating: to lick someone is to thrash them.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquor is strong alcoholic drink such as whisky or gin.

clue.text: Central character, not like Lean der

parts.note: anti means against, not in favour of
Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to his lover Hero, so his beloved is Hero

explanation.surface: A protagonist quite unlike the heroic swimmer Leander of Greek legend.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan breaks Leander across a line as Lean / der. Leander was for Hero, so one not like him is against Hero.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti-hero is a protagonist lacking the usual heroic virtues.

clue.text: School equipment initially used, to produce vulgar art

indicators.note: the equipment is used first, so it comes ahead of the school in the answer

parts.note: kit is equipment, gear

explanation.surface: Pupils' supplies are used to make tacky pictures in class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially used' sets KIT ahead of SCH, though the clue names the school first.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitsch is gaudy, tasteless art with mass appeal.

clue.text: It avoids having to take a shot in the dark

definitions.text: It avoids having to take a shot in the dark

parts.words: It avoids having to take a shot in the dark
parts.note: a shot in the dark sounds like a wild guess, but here it is a photograph taken where there is little light, which this device lights up

explanation.definitionFit: A photographer's lamp that gives a burst of light lets pictures be taken without darkness spoiling them.

clue.text: Vote English politician recorded in real reform, for instance

indicators.note: something recorded in a register is written inside it, so these letters go inside
to reform is to remake, so the letters of real are reshaped

parts.note: X is the mark made on a ballot paper
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: A vote for an English MP is recorded as an example of genuine reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' turns REAL into ELAR, and 'recorded in' puts XEMP after its E.
explanation.definitionFit: An exemplar is an example or model, a case cited as typical.

clue.text: Man watching from box Shylock's first appearance on stage

indicators.note: the first letter of Shylock's name is taken

parts.note: an actor's entry is their arrival on stage

explanation.surface: A man watches from a theatre box as Shylock makes his first entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: The box is a sentry box, not a theatre box.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry is a soldier on guard, often standing in a small hut.
